chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Nu'ayn ibn Shu'ayb from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from one who narrated it from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) said:
"The ribat (military vigil/garrisoning) is three days, and its maximum is forty days; if one exceeds that, it is considered jihad."
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between ribat and jihad in Shia jurisprudence regarding duration?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between temporary ribat (garrisoning) and sustained jihad, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding military service obligations. By setting the threshold at forty days, the Imams delineate the spiritual merit of vigilance from the broader duty of active combat, reflecting the practical realities of early Islamic military campaigns. This distinction underscores the importance of intention and duration in determining the specific religious rulings applicable to the fighter.
